cli.monitor_help.monitor.note: Top-level summary: inspect standing monitors, or cancel one only when its session has no runtime open.

cli.monitor_help.status.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.monitor_help.status.note: status lists all monitors on this machine ordered by their next scheduled check, soonest first.

cli.monitor_help.json.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.monitor_help.json.note: Shared --json help for both status and cancel: output is machine-readable. Preserve the flag token.

cli.monitor_help.cancel.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.monitor_help.cancel.note: cancel is allowed only on a session with no runtime open; a live session changes its own monitors from inside. Preserve this safety restriction.

cli.monitor_help.session.tone: terse, operator-facing, describes a flag or command
cli.monitor_help.session.note: First cancel positional argument identifies the session that owns the monitor.

cli.monitor_help.monitor_id.note: Second cancel positional argument identifies the monitor; m1 and m2 are literal example IDs, not words to translate.
